source: Misc/installer/settings_page.py from settings_page.txt and the game's menu rows

settings.label: Turning
settings.help: Smooth: the turning stick turns you steadily (Turn Speed). Snap: each push turns you at once by the angle.
settings.path: Advanced VR Options > Movement > Locomotion > Turning

settings.label: Turn Speed
settings.help: How fast smooth turning turns you.
settings.path: VR Settings > Comfort, Teleport and Turning > Turn Speed

settings.label: Vignette
settings.help: Darkens the edges of your view while the sticks move or turn you: it eases motion sickness for many. Your own steps in the room never do it.
settings.path: VR Settings > Comfort, Teleport and Turning > Vignette

settings.label: Position
settings.help: Seated: the game stands you up (your eyes at your standing Height), the body stands with its legs on the floor, the holsters and pouches move where a seated player reaches them, and a hand reaching low goes on down to the floor. VR Calibration and Body Calibration take you seated too.
settings.path: VR Settings > Height and Hand Calibration > Seated Play > Position

settings.label: Handedness
settings.help: Sets which stick moves you, the wrist gadget's arm and the flashlight's side together. Left-handed: the right stick moves, the gadget on the right arm, the torch on the right (Custom: set apart, below).
settings.path: Advanced VR Options > Body and Display > Handedness

settings.label: Gloves
settings.help: Leather gloves on your hands: fingerless ones leave the fingertips bare (in your skin tone); full ones cover every finger. With bare forearms (no bracers) a cuff covers the wrist.

settings.label: Body Type
settings.help: How much of your body you see: all of it, legs and all; the torso and arms; or only the hands.
settings.path: VR Settings > Body and Flashlight > Body Type

settings.label: Replace All Humanoids
settings.help: Every grunt and enforcer a map spawns (its own, its spawners', its waiting ones) is its armed version holding its own gun: the same damage, rate of fire, aim, health and loot as the one it replaces, but you can knock or pull the gun out of its hands, win it in a tug, parry it, shoot it out, and its ragdoll keeps hold of it. Takes effect at the next map load (vr_agrunt_repl).
settings.path: Advanced VR Options > Combat > Armed Humanoid Replacements > Replace All Humanoids

settings.label: Gore
settings.help: Over the top: hits spray blood onto the walls, floor and ceiling behind, gibbing paints the room, pools spread under corpses, gibs stick to ceilings and drip.

settings.label: Graphics Presets
settings.help: Off (Quake), Low, Medium, High (as shipped) and Ultra set the settings on the Graphics pages at once; My Settings sets yours back. Also on VR Settings.

choices.label: Off (Quake)
choices.help: Quake's own look: flat dynamic lights, no shadows, bumps, ambient occlusion, bloom or tone mapping, plain liquids, no teleporter views. The least GPU time.

choices.label: Low
choices.help: For weaker graphics cards: Quake VR's lighting and look with few shadows (2 dynamic lights, none from the map), no bumps, parallax, ambient occlusion, refraction, teleporter views or heat haze. About a third of High's GPU time.

choices.label: Medium
choices.help: Most of it at about half High's GPU time: bumps, parallax (without its depth: things meet the wall's surface, not its carved relief), ambient occlusion, every liquid effect and teleporter views, with fewer and smaller shadows (4 dynamic lights, 2 map lights).

choices.label: High (as shipped)
choices.help: The game's defaults: everything on, 8 shadowed dynamic lights and 4 map lights out to 3072 units.

choices.label: Ultra
choices.help: Past the defaults, for fast graphics cards: 12 shadowed dynamic lights and 6 map lights out to 4096 units, more torch lights, particles at full resolution, the finer bloom, deeper parallax steps.
